anya: Heads-up — we saw a perf regression on the quantized FP8 path in prod this morning. 99th latency for short chat requests jumped ~2.3x after yesterday's kernel swap. :eyes:
kevin: ugh. which kernel swap exactly? FP8 GEMM -> fused-atten-gemm-v2?
maria: is KV cache enabled for those requests? that often masks kernel overhead for short tokens.
anya: KV cache was enabled, but cache-hit ratio dropped from 92% -> 60% for that workload. Weird because model input distribution didn't change AFAIK.
sam: can you dump the per-token breakdown from the runtime profiler? trying to see where time moved to (kernel launch vs memcpy vs dequant).
anya: pasted the condensed profiler below (one request, 12 tokens). removed noisy lines.

```
ProfilerSummary:
 token_0: total_ms=12.3  alloc_ms=0.2 memcpy_ms=0.5 kernel_launch_ms=6.7 kernel_exec_ms=3.8 kv_lookup_ms=0.3
 token_1: total_ms=11.8  alloc_ms=0.1 memcpy_ms=0.45 kernel_launch_ms=6.4 kernel_exec_ms=3.5 kv_lookup_ms=0.25
 token_2: total_ms=34.1  alloc_ms=0.2 memcpy_ms=1.2 kernel_launch_ms=8.8 kernel_exec_ms=18.7 kv_lookup_ms=0.9  <-- big spike (dequant+calibration?)
 token_3..11: avg_total_ms=10.9  avg_kernel_launch=5.9 avg_kernel_exec=3.3 avg_kv_lookup=0.2
 kernel_counters: FP8_gemm_calls=1024, INT8_gemm_calls=0, avg_quantize_time_per_call_ms=0.018, dequant_calls=120
 cache_stats: hit_rate=0.60, avg_kv_size_bytes=48k
```

kevin: that token_2 spike looks like a one-off calibration/quant path falling back. Could be a slow path when quant scales are re-computed at runtime. Did we just enable per-batch dynamic calibration?
maria: we rolled dynamic calibration on yesterday for FP8 to fix accuracy drift. It's supposed to run async but maybe it steals GPU time in the serving thread if a fallback occurs.
anya: config shows "fp8.dynamic_calibration=on" and "fp8.calibrate_sync_threshold=1" (sync if batch_size <= 1). Our short chat requests are often single-batch.
sam: ah — that threshold explains it. If single-batch triggers sync calibration, kernel_exec jumps since calibration does a few passes. Should be async for small batches.
kevin: aside from calibration, kernel selection heuristics could choose fused-atten-gemm that does extra pre/post steps for FP8 (casting, scaling). We need finer counters: separate quantize_ms, dequant_ms, scale_compute_ms in profiler.
anya: agreed. Also need KV cache hit attribution in the per-token latency: i.e., if cache miss we should attribute cost to kv_fetch + recompute_gemm. Right now KV lookup is a tiny number even on misses.
maria: proposal: add two new counters surfaced to Console for quantized routes: "quantize_ms", "dequant_ms", "calibration_ms", and a boolean "calibration_blocked" per-request. Also show cache_hit boolean per-token and per-request cache_hit_rate.
sam: and on the kernel side increment kernel_counter labels with kernel_variant (e.g., fp8_fused_v1, fp8_fused_v2, int8_fast) so we can correlate regressions to a specific variant.
kevin: for short-term mitigation: revert "fp8.calibrate_sync_threshold" to 0 (always async) and deploy a flame-safe async queue with backpressure — we shouldn't block hot serving threads.
anya: can we also add a runtime metric that correlates per-route avg_cache_hit_rate with 99th latency over a sliding window? it'd help ops triage whether cache misses or kernel changes are root cause.
maria: yes — Redwood Console can graph that. I'll add a request to the observability board: ticket OBS-4124.
kevin: one more note: INT8 path looks much steadier in internal perf tests. But quant/FP8 gave ~1.6x throughput improvement in best case. So we want to keep FP8 but make calibration non-blocking and improve heuristics for small batches.
anya: agreed. Action items:
- kevin: add kernel_variant counters + quantize/dequant/calibration timings to profiler (PR: runtime#891)
- maria: dashboard panels: per-token cache_hit boolean, per-request calibration_blocked, kernel_variant heatmap (ticket OBS-4124)
- sam: change default fp8.calibrate_sync_threshold=0 and add async calibration queue + guard (PR: serving#270)
- anya: monitor next 48h, capture 99/99.9 latency and cache_hit rate per-route

maria: I'll also add an alert: if cache_hit_rate drops >20% and 99th latency rises >1.5x within 15m, create a page to eng-runtime.
kevin: and add a small micro-benchmark to reproduce the single-batch calibration fallback locally: script snippet below.

```
# reproduce calibration block
python tools/run_small_load.py --model redwood-small-fp8 --batch 1 --requests 200 --seed 42 --enable-fp8-calibration
```

anya: nice. I'll run it and post profiler dumps. If we confirm, we can hotfix config and roll kernel rollback if needed. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: deploy status: canary serving rollout 0.6.7 -> 0.6.8 started, 2/5 hosts updated, no deploy failures.
kevin: cool. let's keep this thread for updates — paste profiler outputs here if you see another spike.
anya: will do. first dump coming in ~30m.
sam: ping me when you have the dump, I'll help correlate kernel_counters to the spike. :mag_right:
